I've been working this land for 40 years. My father farmed before me and his father before that. I don't read agricultural books — I know what works here in Quzhou because I've seen it with my own eyes, season after season.

My 15 mu is split the way I've always done it: 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and 5 mu in cotton on the side. The wheat-maize land I've run this way my whole life. Plant wheat in October after the fall rains, water it through winter and spring, harvest in June. Then right away put in the maize on the same fields, harvest before National Day. That land never rests but it keeps feeding my household.

For the wheat I'll use the improved variety from the seed store in town — the same Jimai type I've used for years. I put fertilizer down at planting and again at jointing. Three waterings: winter water to protect the roots, jointing water for the stalks, and filling water for the grain. Two pesticide passes — one for weeds early, one for rust and aphids in spring. I use the rotary tiller to prep the ground.

For maize I go hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the store has that's similar. I sow it straight into the stubble after wheat, no tilling needed. Two irrigations, maybe three if July is dry. Maize doesn't give me much trouble with pests here.

Cotton is the hard work. Five mu, planted in April. Cotton takes water, takes fertilizer, and the bollworms come every year without fail. I'll spray six times at least — you miss one flush of bollworms and half your crop is gone. I plough that ground in spring before planting.
